Definition: from G2374 and οὖρος (a watcher); a gate- warden:--that kept the door, porter.
BiblicalUsage: thyrōrós stands behind the English phrase a doorkeeper, a porter. In Mark 13:34, commanded the porter to watch, and it appears again in John 10:3.
TheologicalSignificance: A porter told to watch while the master is away reminds me to stay alert, because the return I wait for is certain.
